findings.title: Team permission check uses AND instead of OR
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. A user is either an admin or an owner, never usually both in the sense these helpers test, so the expression is almost always false for a team admin and, despite the variable name, this does not grant admins access. The result is that team admins (and in many membership models owners too, if `isTeamAdmin` returns false for role OWNER) cannot add guests to their team's bookings even though the name/intent says they should. This should be `||`.

findings.title: EventManager built from the caller's credentials, not the booking organizer's
findings.body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` fetches the credentials of the logged-in caller, and the EventManager is constructed with `{...user, credentials}`. Since this endpoint is reachable by attendees and team admins (not just the organizer), the calendar/video update in `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will be attempted with credentials that do not own the external calendar event, so the attendee update silently fails (or targets the wrong account). The credentials and destination calendar should come from the booking's organizer (`booking.user`).

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails receives the raw input list instead of the actually-added guests
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the unfiltered input array. In `email-manager.ts` this list decides who receives the "you were invited" (`AttendeeScheduledEmail`) vs the "guests added" notice. Any email the caller submitted that was already an attendee (filtered out into `uniqueGuests`) will therefore receive a brand-new booking confirmation email again instead of the add-guests notification. `uniqueGuests` should be passed instead.

findings.title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive, allowing bypass and duplicate attendees
findings.body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lower-cased but the incoming `guest` string is not, so `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` can be trivially bypassed by submitting a different case (e.g. `Spam@Example.com`). The same case-sensitivity applies to the existing-attendee comparison `guest === attendee.email`, so the same address in a different case is inserted again, producing duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails. Both comparisons should normalize case.

findings.title: No limit or de-duplication on the guests array server-side
findings.body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no max length and no uniqueness constraint; the uniqueness/validity checks only exist client-side in `AddGuestsDialog`. Any authenticated user who is an attendee of a booking can POST hundreds of arbitrary addresses and the handler will create an attendee row and send a booking email to each one, turning the endpoint into an email-sending relay (spam/abuse vector) and bloating the booking's attendee list. Add a `.max(...)` bound and de-duplicate (case-insensitively) in the schema/handler.

findings.title: No validation of booking status or time before adding guests
findings.body: The handler accepts any `bookingId` and never checks `booking.status` or whether the booking is in the past. The UI only exposes the action for upcoming/confirmed bookings, but the tRPC mutation is directly callable, so guests can be added to CANCELLED/REJECTED or long-past bookings, which then triggers confirmation/ics emails for an event that no longer exists. It also does not account for `seatsPerTimeSlot`: adding attendees to a seated event bypasses the seat limit and creates attendees with no seat reference.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event type disableStandardEmails settings
findings.body: Unlike every other sender in this file (e.g. `sendLocationChangeEmails`), `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no `eventTypeMetadata` and never calls `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`. Event types configured with `disableStandardEmails.all.host`/`.attendee` will still send host and attendee emails when guests are added, violating the user's explicit email-suppression setting.

findings.title: Team hosts never notified because the CalendarEvent has no team data
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails` loops over `calendarEvent.team?.members` to notify co-hosts, but the `evt` built in `addGuests.handler.ts` never populates `team` (the booking query selects `eventType` without team/hosts). For team events, only the primary organizer is emailed and the branch is dead code.

findings.title: Subject line dereferences attendees[0] without a guard
findings.body: `name: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` will throw a TypeError if `calEvent.attendees` is empty, which would reject the whole `sendAddGuestsEmails` promise chain. Other organizer templates guard this; use optional access or fall back to the organizer/team name.

findings.title: Email failure swallowed without the error details
findings.body: `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` discards `err`, so a mail delivery or template failure leaves no diagnosable trace. Use the project `logger` and include `safeStringify(err)` plus the booking id.

findings.title: Invalid-email banner is never cleared and empty submit is a silent no-op
findings.body: `setIsInvalidEmail(false)` is only called by the Cancel button; on a successful mutation (or when the user corrects the input) the flag stays true, so the red "Emails must be unique and valid" message is still displayed the next time the dialog is opened via the dropdown. Additionally, when the user removes all email rows, `handleAdd` returns early with no toast or message, so clicking "Add" appears to do nothing.

findings.title: New UI component imports from its own package barrel, creating a cycle
findings.body: `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx` imports `Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip` from `@calcom/ui`, while `packages/ui/index.tsx` re-exports this very module (via `MultiEmailLazy`). This self-referential cycle can resolve to `undefined` components at runtime depending on module evaluation order/bundler, producing "Element type is invalid" render errors. Import the components by relative path (as the sibling form components do) instead of through the package barrel.

findings.title: No tests for the new addGuests mutation
findings.body: The PR adds a new authenticated mutation that writes attendees and sends emails, with non-trivial authorization logic (organizer / attendee / team admin), blacklist filtering and duplicate filtering, but no unit or integration tests were added. Regressions in the permission branches would silently allow or deny guest additions; the AND/OR bug in the team check is exactly the kind of defect a test would have caught.
